A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study with the same title and authors. All 36 pages of v1 and 40 pages of v2, including Appendices A–D, provide readable text, equations, figures, and references sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CelebA experiments measuring FID, memorization, and losses, plus Gaussian-mixture and random-feature simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds conditional-generation, optimizer, and covariance-spectrum experiments.

M1.justification: The principal RFNN architecture and unconditional score-learning procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds a class-conditioned Gaussian-mixture diffusion model using classifier-free guidance, introducing conditioning inputs and a guided-generation adaptation.

E1.justification: CelebA, Gaussian-mixture, and Gaussian random-feature data remain the principal coverage. v2 adds class-conditional Gaussian-mixture generation in Appendix B.3 and a non-isotropic covariance scenario in Figure 4, extending the tested conditions without introducing a new real-world dataset.

E2.justification: Optimizer-comparison membership changes: Adam is newly evaluated in the CelebA and RFNN analyses, while the GMM Adam comparison in v1 Appendix B.3 and Figure 11 is removed. Adam itself was already evaluated in v1; these are changes to where it is compared with SGD.

E3.justification: Section 2 expands the width sweep from {16,32,64} to {8,16,32,48,64} and introduces estimation of the architectural threshold using 2M-update behavior. New experiments include CelebA Adam training at W=64 and learning rate 10^-4, and conditional GMM evaluation at W=64 with n={256,512,1024}. The established FID and loss-evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens checks of the proposed mechanism through Adam experiments on CelebA and RFNNs, conditional-generation scaling, non-isotropic spectral validation, and empirical estimation of the architectural-regularization boundary. The earlier GMM Adam analysis is removed. Existing full-batch, diffusion-time, and scalar-variance analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report twice-standard-deviation bars over five FID test sets or loss-noise realizations, 95% memorization intervals using 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and RFNN score-error bars using three standard deviations over ten runs. No changed uncertainty procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds conditional-generation, Adam, anisotropic-spectrum, and architectural-threshold results, and revises Figure 3's phase boundaries. For the matched CelebA illustration at n=1024, W=32, and 1.62M updates, memorization changes from 47.2% in v1 Figure 7 to 34.1% in v2 Figure 6, although v2 Appendix A.1 still states 47.2%. This establishes inconsistent revised reporting, not a demonstrated performance improvement. The main-text score-error exponent is also aligned with the approximately 0.59 estimate already present in v1 Appendix D.

T1.justification: The theory expands from isotropic Gaussian data to stated sub-Gaussian assumptions with bounded general covariance. Theorem 3.1 changes from two resolvent equations to a covariance-dependent three-equation system. Theorem 3.2 and Appendix C add population-spectrum characterization, a bulk-scaling lemma, and substantially revised Gaussian-equivalence, replica, and fast-timescale derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution statements retain the same two-timescale mechanism: generation time is independent of dataset size, memorization time grows linearly with it, and early stopping enables generalization despite overparameterization. The added experiments support this retained claim.

C2.justification: v2 explains the fast spectral bulk through population covariance, qualifies approximate capacity-independence to W>8, and discusses conditioning-dependent timescales and possible class-specific intermediate regimes. It adds heavy-tailed-data and conditional-generation limitations, and explicitly defers a more rigorous treatment of the generalized Gaussian-equivalence argument in Appendix C.3.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, CelebA Adam hyperparameters, PyTorch implementation attribution, and explicit threshold values for checks already mentioned in v1. However, its new Section 2 channel multipliers {1,2,3} conflict with the retained {1,2,4} in Appendix A.1; the PDFs do not establish an actual backbone change.

R1.justification: The main related-work narrative is retained. v2 adds references supporting conditional guidance, covariance theory, universality, and heavy-tailed limitations, and gives a formal citation to Favero, Sclocchi, and Wyart's related work previously mentioned only in acknowledgments. The Hermite-polynomial reference changes from Wikipedia to Bach.

P1.justification: The overall main-text sequence and Appendices A–D are retained. Local revisions separate theoretical assumptions, clarify evaluation and timescale explanations, reorganize limitations into bullets, revise appendix subsections, and update author information. These changes refine the narrative without comprehensively restructuring it.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a NeurIPS layout with redesigned title and author blocks, typography, and text width. Figures are substantially reorganized: Figure 2 gains sample-neighbor panels, Figure 3 is redrawn, the RFNN schematic and spectra are combined, and appendix optimizer and conditional-generation displays are added or replaced. These changes extend beyond renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the already-supported central result with Adam validation on CelebA and RFNNs, conditional-generation evidence, broader covariance analysis, and documented code access. These benefits are tempered by the deferred rigorous justification of the generalized Gaussian-equivalence argument and new inconsistencies in the memorization percentage and U-Net specification. The evidence supports a useful but limited net quality improvement.
